newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO condemns closure of its Washington office.
newsitem.headline: PLO condemns closure of its Washington office.

text.p: Palestinian officials on Wednesday condemned the temporary closure of the PLO's Washington office and said it was a severe blow to American efforts to revive the stalled peace process.

The Palestine Liberation Organisation office suspended its operations at midnight on Tuesday. Congress allowed its permit to expire by not passing its annual foreign aid bill as planned before the summer recess.

The Middle East Peace Facilitation Act, providing funds for the Palestinian Authority and allowing the PLO to operate an office under its name in Washington, is part of that bill. It will be taken up after Congress resumes in September.

"It is a seriously wrong decision at this particular time when (U.S. special envoy Dennis) Ross is here trying to revive the peace process. It is only adding fuel to the fire," senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.
"It is a severe blow to Ross's efforts and we hope the U.S. administration would work to revoke this decision immediately. We were told by the administration that it would do so."
The PLO's representative in Washington, Hassan Abdel-Rahman, told Voice of Palestine Radio the suspension "was a negative message to the Palestinians and harms the peace process".
Abdel-Rahman said he expected his office to resume its operations in September.
Other officials said earlier in Washington that they would continue to turn up for work, as with two earlier lapses in authority in previous years, but would not technically represent the PLO.

The PLO has had a representative office in Washington since 1979 under various names. The office became the official PLO representative office in 1993 after Israel and the PLO signed the Oslo interim peace accords.
State Department spokesman James Rubin said the suspension would not interfere with contacts between the United States government and the Palestinian leadership.

Ross has held four separate meetings with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an effort to restart peace talks deadlocked since March after Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Ross's mission focused on restoring security coordination following a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem on July 30. He told reporters on Tuesday that the process "has been set in motion".

"Suspending the operations of the PLO office is another message from Congress to the Palestinian people that it adopts the position of the far right in Israel and this does not serve U.S. interests in the region," said negotiator Hassan Asfour.
"This will only increase the Palestinian people's hostility towards America," he said.
